This hypothesis is derived from the dataset, which includes education expenditure as a percentage of GNI and GNI per capita (constant 2015 US dollar) for Sub-Saharan Africa and Lower middle income countries from 1975 to 2015. The relationship between these variables was found to be statistically significant with a correlation coefficient of approximately -0.966, indicating a strong negative correlation.
